title: Flexing RISC-V Instruction Subset Processors to Extreme Edge
problem: Extreme edge applications (smart labels, wearable healthcare, smart textiles) require processors that are ultra-low area, ultra-low power, conformable, and low-cost—properties that conventional silicon RISC-V processors and existing smallest designs like Serv cannot meet—while still supporting programmability for occasional firmware updates.
motivation: The extreme edge application space (wearables, disposable IoT, flexible electronics) demands flexible integrated circuits (FlexICs) on polyimide substrates operating in the kHz range; metal-oxide IGZO transistor technology has dramatically lower carbon footprint than silicon but requires minimal gate counts, making a full ISA implementation impractical.
method: The approach analyzes an application to identify which instructions from the full RISC-V instruction set (RV32E) it needs—typically 24-86% of the total—then assembles pre-built, formally verified hardware blocks for those instructions from a library into a Modular Execution Unit (ModularEX) using a switch statement. The combined hardware is synthesized (converted to a physical chip layout) with commercial tools (Synopsys ICC2 or Cadence Innovus) on Pragmatic Semiconductor's 0.6-micron IGZO FlexIC process (a technology for making low-area, flexible chips), and the synthesis automatically eliminates unused logic gates. A single-cycle, non-pipelined microarchitecture (where each instruction completes in one clock step, rather than overlapping multiple instructions) suffices for the kilohertz performance requirements of extreme-edge devices. For applications that need firmware updates later, an AI tool rewrites any instructions outside the chosen subset using equivalent instructions from within it.
key_novelty: The core idea is using a library of formally pre-verified instruction-sized hardware blocks that can be automatically assembled into minimal-area processors on the FlexIC process, eliminating per-application design and verification cycles.
contributions: RISSP generation methodology with a pre-verified full ISA hardware library where each instruction is a discrete, formally verified RTL block
Physical FlexIC implementation of three extreme edge application-specific RISSPs achieving up to 42% area and 21% power reduction over full RISC-V
RISSPs are ~40x more energy-efficient than Serv (world's smallest 32-bit RISC-V) due to Serv's high flip-flop proportion and bit-serial CPI of 32
Generative AI-based assembly retargeting tool for updating long-lasting RISSP firmware without recompiling to unsupported instructions

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: ~40x more energy-efficient per instruction than Serv
metrics.area: 8-43% area reduction vs. full RV32E processor (synthesis); up to 42% reduction in FlexIC physical implementation
metrics.ppa: 3-30% power reduction vs. full RISC-V; up to 21% in physical FlexIC; max frequency 1500-1850 kHz on 0.6-um IGZO process
metrics.other: Applications use only 24-86% of full RV32E ISA (9-32 distinct instructions at -O2)

baselines: RISSP-RV32E (full RV32E processor generated by same methodology)
limitations: RISSPs are not directly compatible with applications that use instructions outside their subset; the generative AI retargeting tool addresses this for long-lasting applications but adds toolchain complexity, and single-cycle non-pipelined design limits clock frequency on conventional silicon.
primary_theme: automated RISC-V instruction-subset processor generation for flexible extreme-edge electronics
